claim: Tree search with a model-judged value beat flat sampling on Game of 24 with GPT-4 in the original paper (ToT b=5 74% vs CoT-SC 9%, best-of-100 CoT 49%), but the number is author-run on 100 games.
agent_test: Rerun on 100 Game-of-24-style items at equal total tokens: tree vs best-of-N with code verifier.

claim: Independent reruns put ToT lower than 74%: 69% (AoT, GPT-4, b=5), 72% (GPT-3.5 evaluator) to 76% (GPT-4 evaluator) at b=5 and 77% at b=3 (Wang), 20% for GPT-3.5 (LATS vs 19% original). Order of magnitude holds, exact value varies by 5-8 points.
agent_test: Log variance over 3 seeds before claiming any tree gain of under 8 points.

claim: Most of ToT's Game-of-24 gain comes from a checkable sure/impossible pruner on a tiny step space: best-of-150 direct queries with a sound code verifier reach 70%, and LLM-written successor and goal-test code with plain BFS solves 1361/1362 problems (100%) in seconds. Gap search: the crossword result assumes 10 candidate answers per clue including the right one.
agent_test: On tasks with a codable check, compare tree vs code-verified sampling vs code search at equal tokens.

claim: Quality of the state evaluator decides whether tree search works: random evaluator drops Game of 24 Top1 from 0.74 to 0.0; GPT-3.5 evaluator with GPT-4 proposer keeps 0.68-0.72; weak generator is the bottleneck (GPT-3.5 gen + GPT-4 eval 0.30-0.31).
agent_test: Ablate evaluator (code, strong model, weak model, random) inside S6; spend on generator first.

claim: Prompted LLM self-evaluation is a weak state value: a learned value function lifts Game24 Path@1 from 21.0 (GPT-3.5 prompted) to 64.8, and tree search needs a discriminator of about 90% accuracy to beat re-ranking; intrinsic self-correction lowers accuracy. Gap search: ProcessBench shows step-judging F1 varies widely by judge and difficulty (o1-mini 87.9 vs GPT-4o 61.9 average), and Huang finds no-oracle self-correction lowers CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 41.8.
agent_test: Measure judge accuracy on labelled partial states first; only branch if judge accuracy is high or a code check exists.

claim: Tree search is 10-20x slower than re-ranking with negligible gain when discriminators are LLM-based (text-to-SQL, math).
agent_test: Equal-token comparison on our tasks with the judge in the loop.

claim: At matched budgets sampling plus voting or reranking is usually as good as or better than tree search for short-horizon tasks: CoT-SC with reward model 52.3 vs BFS-V 52.5 on GSM8K; SC beats ToT on GPT-3.5; Xie's equal-cost gain is 4.3 points. Gap search: on reasoning models, majority voting beat PlanSearch, mixture of agents and revisions (Wang 2025); parallel beat extended single chains at equal tokens (Ghosal 2025, Zeng 2025). Counter: Sharma 2025 finds sequential wins 43/45 with a 4096-token chain cap.
agent_test: Default to sample and select; branch only when a trigger fires.

claim: Search helps most when the plan is deep or the first step is a bottleneck: about 60% of CoT chains die at step 1 on Game of 24; PrOntoQA 48.8 to 94.4 and Game24 12.7 to 64.8 with search; Blocksworld RAP gains persist to 6 steps but fall with length (0.32 at 10 steps).
agent_test: Trigger tree only after a cheap step-1 check or low-agreement signal; cap depth.

claim: Search against a process reward model is difficulty dependent: beam search beats best-of-N at levels 3-4 and small budgets, hurts at levels 1-2 and at large budgets (PRM over-optimisation); compute-optimal allocation matches best-of-N with about 4x less compute. Gap search: AB-MCTS shows the best arm flips with budget (sampling wins at 128 on ARC, plateaus by 200-500).
agent_test: Route by difficulty estimate (model-estimated bins), not by a fixed schedule.

claim: Cheap rollout-free tree search (REBASE) beats MCTS and sampling on cost: Llemma-7B+REBASE beats Llemma-34B, about 2x fewer FLOPs at equal accuracy; MCTS wastes tokens on unfinished solutions. DeepSeek-R1 also reports MCTS failing in token space.
agent_test: Prefer reward-balanced expansion with many finished branches over MCTS rollouts.

claim: Writing the search trace into one prompt (Algorithm of Thoughts) matches multi-call ToT at about 1% of the queries: 71% with 1 query vs ToT 69% with 109 queries; crosswords 52% vs 46.5%.
agent_test: Compare one-call trace prompt vs tree loop at equal tokens on two non-arithmetic tasks.

claim: Graph moves (aggregate/merge, refine) beat trees on tasks that split into subtasks: sorting median error 61% lower than ToT at P=64, cost 31% lower; the gain comes from decomposition, and it vanishes at small sizes (P=32). Gap search: GoT tested only GPT-3.5, has no split-merge-without-scoring arm, and the authors attribute the gain to decomposition.
agent_test: Test a code-run merge step on a decomposable task of two sizes.

claim: Training on search traces with dead ends and backtracking beats optimal-path training (Countdown 51.27% vs 25.73%; Searchformer 93.7% optimal on Sokoban), but only with training, not by prompting.
agent_test: Not testable without training; nearest prompt analogue is feeding back real failed attempts (G2).

claim: Search over natural-language plans adds diversity that raises pass@k: PlanSearch 77.0% pass@200 vs 60.6% repeated sampling on LiveCodeBench; gain tracks idea diversity.
agent_test: Add a plan-diversity step before code and measure pass@k at equal tokens.

claim: Search over real web actions improves agents but needs reversibility: VWA 18.9 to 26.4 (+39.7%), WA 15.0 to 19.2 (+28.0%), gains rising with budget; absolute scores stay low.
agent_test: Limit tree to reversible steps; block expansion through irreversible actions.

claim: LLM-guided ToT, RAP and LATS are neither sound nor complete and cost far more LLM calls than code search; LATS ablation: no LM heuristic 0.37, DFS 0.42, no reflection 0.58, full 0.63 on HotpotQA. Gap search: Katz estimates $14,000 (RAP) and $16,000 (LATS) vs $40 for IO/CoT on the same suites.
agent_test: Ablate value heuristic and reflection separately at equal nodes.

claim: ToT on open-ended writing gives a small gain judged by GPT-4 (7.56 vs 6.93 CoT) with iterative refine on IO close behind (7.67); no study opened tests ideation novelty with human raters. Gap search: blind human raters (79 experts) rate scaled LLM ideas more novel (5.64 vs 4.84) but the pipeline is flat overgenerate-and-rank, not a tree.
agent_test: Blind human or multi-judge novelty rating, length-normalised, at equal tokens.

claim: Stronger base model without search can beat weaker model with search: GSM8K CoT GPT-4 92.0 vs search+PAL Codex 80.2; ToT adds little (GSM8K 90 vs 86, StrategyQA 83 vs 82) where the model already does well.
agent_test: Check base-model accuracy first; skip search when above a threshold.

claim: Small models with MCTS and cross-checking gain a lot (rStar GSM8K LLaMA2-7B 12.51 to 63.91), but baseline is few-shot CoT only and not compared at equal tokens.
agent_test: Equal-token rerun against self-consistency before adoption.

claim: With a prompted value and an equal tool-and-token budget, a value-guided tree beat budget-matched majority voting on a reasoning model (GPT-OSS-20B) on four multi-hop QA sets, but only with the value signal: a tree with random expansion was worse than voting (0.215 vs 0.268 EM).
agent_test: Replicate on our tasks: tree with value vs random tree vs voting at equal tokens; keep the random-tree arm.

claim: On R1-distilled reasoning models with prompted judges, simple majority voting equals or beats search and revision methods (PlanSearch, mixture of agents, revisions); sample diversity is the better spend. No o-series or Claude-thinking tree-vs-voting test was found.
agent_test: Default to sample-and-vote for reasoning-model tasks; branch only when a check exists or a trigger fires.

claim: Whether parallel or sequential refinement wins at equal tokens depends on per-chain caps: Sharma finds sequential wins 43/45 with 4096-token chains (about 30 questions per AIME set), while Zeng and Ghosal find parallel better with uncapped chains.
agent_test: Run both arms with uncapped chains and report per-chain token use.

claim: Step judges are only as good as the task allows: first-error F1 ranges from 87.9 (o1-mini) to 61.9 (GPT-4o) averaged over four math sets and falls on olympiad problems; 32.2% of correct-answer solutions on OlympiadBench still hold a process error; idea-quality judges score 43-53% against a 56% human baseline.
agent_test: Before branching on a judge, score it on 20-50 labelled items from the task; branch only above a task-set threshold (Chen: about 90%).

claim: Adaptive width/depth trees (AB-MCTS) beat repeated sampling by 1-3 points on code with a sound test signal at budget 128, lose to it on ARC-AGI at that budget, and overtake it only at larger budgets (200-500) once sampling plateaus.
agent_test: Trigger deeper search on observed sampling plateau and a sound score, not from the start.

claim: Human-rated novelty gain for LLM ideation exists for flat overgenerate-and-rank (5.64 vs 4.84, N=49 ideas per arm, blind), but 4000 samples collapse to about 200 unique ideas and the best prompted ranker is 53.3% accurate; no opened study tests an idea tree against sample-and-rank with human raters.
agent_test: Run tree vs sample-rank-dedup with blind multi-rater novelty at equal tokens; dedup before scoring.

claim: Code-written successor and goal-test search is a formalisability test: GPT-4 needed 1.0-2.8 rounds in four rule-bound domains, and the GIF-MCTS authors state the method needs deterministic, fully observable tasks. Open-ended, stochastic or hidden-state tasks lack a unit oracle and cannot be formalised this way.
agent_test: Gate: attempt successor and goal test in at most 3 rounds against 3 labelled cases; fall back to sampling if it fails.

claim: Graph-of-thought gains have no ablation separating decomposition, scoring and refinement; the authors credit decomposition, and gains are absent at P=32. The smallest test is split, solve, code-merge with no scoring.
agent_test: Compare code-merge-only vs GoT on sorting and set intersection at P=32, 64, 128.

claim: Breadth above about 3 stops helping probably because samples duplicate (200 unique of 4000 ideas) and instruct models repeat failures (baseline EM 0.289 to 0.293 with budget); this is an inference, not a tested cause.
agent_test: Measure unique-answer count per branch set; stop widening when new unique answers per sample fall under a threshold.
